title: Security Deposit Credit History Judged Across the Customer
content:
For every Security Deposit, credit history is judged across the customer, not only the secured service agreement. Three rules follow from this.

1. **Disconnections count against every deposit.** A disconnection for nonpayment on any of the customer's service agreements during the review period counts against the refund of every deposit the customer holds. Disconnections in a review period are counted as the reconnection charges posted on any of the customer's service agreements in the period, plus one for each of the customer's agreements currently in disconnected status. The review period is the kind's review months ending on the deposit's refund review date.
2. **Prior Lakeshore history.** The prior Lakeshore history waiver counts any closed agreement of the same customer.
3. **Application at closure.** A deposit applied at closure meets the closing agreement's final balance first, then the unpaid balance of any other closed agreement of the same customer, and only the remainder is refunded.

## Illustrations (hypothetical customer)

A residential customer holds a Residential New Service Deposit on agreement A, whose 12-month review period ends on its refund review date. The customer also has agreement B at a second address.

| Record in A's review period | Disconnections counted against the refund of the deposit on A |
|---|---|
| No reconnection charge on A or B; neither agreement disconnected now | 0 |
| One reconnection charge posted on B; neither agreement disconnected now | 1 |
| No reconnection charge; B currently in disconnected status | 1 |
| One reconnection charge posted on A and B currently disconnected | 2 |

If, hypothetically, the deposit on A is instead applied when A closes, and closed agreement C of the same customer still carries an unpaid balance, the deposit meets A's final balance first, then C's unpaid balance, and only what remains is refunded.
